column1: # ZAP baseline rule configuration.
# Format: <rule id>
# The baseline scan is passive: it reads responses, it does not attack. Every
# rule not listed here keeps its default, and the job fails on any alert at
# WARN or above, so silence here means "we did not decide" rather than
# "we accepted it".
# Only rules with a reason are listed. An IGNORE without one is how a scanner
# quietly stops reporting things that matter.
# 10015 Incomplete or No Cache-control Header
#   Applies to static assets, which are deliberately cacheable for 300s. Every
#   response carrying account or transaction data sets no-store, and that is
#   asserted directly by WEBSEC-006 in SecurityHeadersTest rather than left to
#   the scanner.

column3: Static assets are intentionally cacheable; account data sets no-store (WEBSEC-006)

column1: # 10063 Permissions Policy Header Not Set
#   Set on the application shell, which is the document the policy governs.
#   ZAP also raises it against JSON API responses, where a permissions policy
#   has no meaning.

column3: Set on the document; not meaningful on JSON responses (WEBSEC-009)

column1: # 90005 Sec-Fetch-Dest Header Is Not Set
#   A request header the client sends, not something the server controls.

column3: Client-sent request header, outside the application's control

column1: # 10038 Content Security Policy Header Not Set
#   Kept reportable on purpose. The policy IS set, but if a future response
#   path is added without it this must surface rather than pass quietly.

column3: CSP is set; keep reporting so a new uncovered response path is noticed

column1: # 10098 Cross-Domain Misconfiguration
#   The static shell carries Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * from the hosting
#   platform's static file serving, which the application cannot remove. It is
#   public markup with no credentials. The API grants no origin at all, which
#   is what WEBSEC-005 requires and what SecurityHeadersTest asserts.

column3: Platform wildcard on public static files; the API grants no origin (WEBSEC-005)

column1: # 10055 CSP: script-src unsafe-inline / style-src unsafe-inline
#   The known limitation recorded against WEBSEC-001 in the requirements
#   catalog, not a finding this scan discovered. The interface attaches 84
#   event handlers inline in markup and uses inline style attributes; an
#   inline handler cannot run without unsafe-inline, and a nonce does not
#   help because nonces apply to <script> elements and not to handler
#   attributes. The policy still blocks external script, plugins and
#   base-tag injection. Closing this means moving every handler to
#   addEventListener, which is application work rather than configuration.
#   SecurityHeadersTest asserts the weakness stays confined to this one
#   directive: 'unsafe-eval' or a wildcard source cannot join it unnoticed.

column3: Documented WEBSEC-001 limitation; inline handlers require it, and a test stops it spreading

column1: # 10049 Non-Storable Content
#   Reports that responses cannot be cached, which is the intent. Account and
#   transaction data sets no-store deliberately (WEBSEC-006). This alert
#   fires because the application is doing the right thing.

column3: Non-storable is the intended behaviour for account data (WEBSEC-006)

column1: # 10109 Modern Web Application
#   Informational. It observes that the target is a single-page application
#   and that links may be handled in script. True, and not a defect.

column3: Informational SPA detection, not a finding

column1: # 10027 Information Disclosure - Suspicious Comments
#   Triggered by ordinary words in the client source: select, admin,
#   password as identifiers, and BUG where a comment cites a defect id such
#   as BUG-UI-002.
#   Accepted with a caveat worth stating rather than hiding: public/app.js
#   ships unminified, so its developer comments are readable by anyone. For
#   this project that is close to a feature, since the source is the
#   portfolio. A production bank would strip comments at build time, and
#   there is no frontend build step here to do it.

column3: Application identifiers and defect ids in comments; unminified source is accepted here
